tldr: November's continual-learning papers started with cheaper adapters: RASP (Nov 2) keeps one fixed-size LoRA instead of a branch per session, and a Nov 9 paper shares one prompt across tasks with no rehearsal data. On Nov 18 the thread moved toward deployment, adding specialist vision models to a trained agent's tools and running continual learning on edge devices.
whats_new: Nov 19: two papers carry continual learning into reinforcement learning, one choosing replay by policy improvement and the other using grid-cell-inspired successor features as a reusable basis across changing tasks.
why_it_matters: Updating a deployed model or agent without retraining or regressions is the cost problem here; fixed-size adapters, incremental tool addition and targeted replay are the candidate mechanisms.

status.detail: Six arXiv papers in November on a shared theme rather than one event; all research-stage, none shipped in a product or framework.

beats.headline: Fixed-cost adapters replace per-task growth
beats.summary: Two vision-transformer papers bound parameter cost: one stationary-size LoRA, then one shared prompt with no replay buffer.

beats.headline: Continual learning reaches agent tool spaces and edge hardware
beats.summary: Incremental tool addition for multimodal agents and an end-to-end edge platform, both on Nov 18.

beats.headline: The thread branches into continual reinforcement learning
beats.summary: Two Nov 19 papers target agents whose task changes: replay chosen by policy improvement, and successor features built on a grid-cell basis.

open_questions: Does the tool-space extension paper show that adding a specialist model leaves existing tool-use accuracy unchanged?
Do RASP or the single-prompt method report results beyond vision transformers, on LLMs?
Does Hypnos release code or report on-device memory and latency figures?
Do the continual RL papers test on language-model agents, or only on classic RL environments?
take_for_builders: Do not adopt yet; if you add tools or fine-tune adapters on a live agent, rerun the old task evals after each update to catch regressions.
